title: AdaSAM: Boosting Sharpness-Aware Minimization with Adaptive Learning Rate and Momentum for Training Deep Neural Networks
main_claims: AdaSAM, which combines SAM with adaptive learning rate (AMSGrad-style) and momentum, achieves an O(1/√(bT)) convergence rate in the stochastic non-convex setting.
AdaSAM achieves linear speedup with respect to mini-batch size b, making it theoretically favorable for large-batch training.
Empirical experiments on GLUE benchmark with RoBERTa show AdaSAM outperforms SGD, AMSGrad, and SAM on 6 of 8 tasks.
methodology: The convergence analysis decouples the three coupled steps (perturbation, adaptive learning rate, momentum) using a delayed second-order momentum term and an auxiliary sequence. Assumptions include L-smoothness, bounded variance, and bounded stochastic gradients. The algorithm follows SAM's perturbation step followed by AMSGrad-style adaptive rate update with momentum. Experiments apply AdaSAM to RoBERTa fine-tuning on the GLUE benchmark.
key_results: AdaSAM admits O(1/√(bT)) convergence rate, achieving linear speedup with batch size b.
AdaSAM wins 6 of 8 GLUE tasks compared to SGD, AMSGrad, and SAM in NLP fine-tuning experiments.
AdaSAM recovers SAM when β2=1 (no adaptive learning rate), demonstrating the generality of the analysis.
limitations: Theoretical analysis requires bounded gradient assumption (∥∇fi(x)∥∞ ≤ G), which can be overly restrictive.
Experiments are limited to NLP (GLUE/RoBERTa) fine-tuning; no vision or OOD generalization experiments are reported.
The convergence rate O(1/√(bT)) matches SGD and does not provide a theoretical advantage over base optimizers with respect to iteration complexity.
relevance_to_rq: Peripheral to the core RQ: provides convergence theory for SAM variants but does not study OOD generalization, CIFAR-C, or representation stability. The adaptive SAM formulation is not used in the RQ's experimental design (which uses vanilla SAM with SGD base optimizer).
